title: Move between branches

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Now that we have a `map` branch, let's move to it.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: `git switch map` moves your HEAD to the map branch.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: And `git switch -c <name>` makes a new branch and moves to it in one go.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: One more. You will see `git checkout -b <name>` in older guides everywhere.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: It does the same thing as `switch -c`. `switch` is just the newer, clearer name.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Try both, so neither one surprises you later.

items.text: Create and move to a schedule branch with git switch -c
Do the same with the older git checkout -b, for a food branch

hints: Visit the existing branch, then make two new ones: one with switch, one with checkout.
`git switch <name>` moves. `git switch -c <name>` creates and moves. `git checkout -b <name>` is the older way to create and move.
Run `git switch map`, then `git switch -c schedule`, then `git checkout -b food`.
recap: `git switch <branch>` moves to a branch. `git switch -c <branch>` creates and moves. Older guides write that as `git checkout -b <branch>`: same result.
